Automakers Urge Ban on Chinese Connected Vehicles in US

A coalition of automakers has urged the US Congress to enact a permanent ban on connected vehicles manufactured by Chinese companies. The group argues that these vehicles pose significant national security and data privacy risks due to their potential for surveillance and data collection. They are calling for legislative action to prevent the widespread adoption of Chinese-made connected car technology within the United States, citing concerns over intellectual property and economic competition.
